title: Componentwise normalization over an open with normal reduction
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], let q:T to Spec k be finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let U be a dense open of T. Suppose every stalk of the reduction U_red [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write n:N to T for the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. There is an isomorphism from the inverse image of U in N to U_red, whose composite with the reduction closed immersion U_red to U is n restricted to U. This is only a local normalization compatibility statement and contains neither an arbitrary normal cover nor any geometric normality assertion.

proof.text: Finite type over k makes T Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components. The reduction R of U is locally Noetherian, and its reduction closed immersion is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces.

source.place: Tags 035Q and 0CDV; normal components and normalization over the normal locus

proof.text: A locally Noetherian scheme with domain stalks has open irreducible components: its connected components are open, and the source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_of_isDomain_stalk makes each connected open irreducible. Maximality identifies these with irreducible components. Distinct components are disjoint, since a nonempty open intersection is dense in either irreducible component. For an integral closed component C of T, its restriction over dense U factors through R. The factor is closed, surjective onto one component of R, and is an open immersion: factor through its open image, then apply the reduced-target surjective closed-immersion criterion.

source.place: Tags 035Q and 0CDV; normal components and normalization over the normal locus

proof.text: Transfer integral closedness along the open-immersion stalk isomorphisms from R to the relevant open of C. The source theorem Scheme.isIso_fromNormalization_restrict makes the function-field normalization of C an isomorphism over this open. Thus each normalized component restricted above U maps openly into R. Its range is exactly the inverse image in R of the corresponding component of T.

source.place: Tags 035Q and 0CDV; normal components and normalization over the normal locus

proof.text: The component images in R cover R. They are pairwise distinct: equality of their ranges pulls back along the reduction homeomorphism to equality of the intersections with U, and closing their images in T recovers the original components because U is dense. They are therefore pairwise disjoint open components. The coproduct of these open immersions is an isomorphism by Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of.

source.place: Tags 035Q and 0CDV; normal components and normalization over the normal locus

proof.text: Finite coproducts of schemes are universal. Their pullback along U to T is consequently the coproduct of the restricted normalized components. Compose its inverse comparison with the preceding coproduct isomorphism onto R. Check the displayed equation over U after precomposing each coprojection, using the nilradical lift factorization. This includes the empty coproduct case.

theorem reducedNormalization_over_normal_reduction
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (T : Scheme.{u}) (q : T ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [QuasiCompact q]
    (U : T.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set T))
    (hnormal : ∀ z : U.toScheme.nilradical.subscheme,
      IsDomain (U.toScheme.nilradical.subscheme.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
        IsIntegrallyClosed (U.toScheme.nilradical.subscheme.presheaf.stalk z)) :
    ∃ e : (T.fromReducedNormalization ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ≅ U.toScheme.nilradical.subscheme,
      e.hom ≫ U.toScheme.nilradical.subschemeι = T.fromReducedNormalization ∣_ U
